finding.claim: Loose == comparison of stored reset token lets a password reset succeed without the token when $token is a non-string (e.g. JSON boolean true) or a numeric-equal string. Severity HIGH (downgraded from CRITICAL: unauthenticated reachability unconfirmed because the caller is not in the repo).
finding.sink: Password update UPDATE users SET pw (reset.php:5-6), gated by the comparison at reset.php:4

trace.note: Fetches stored token for $email via quoted query; a reset row must exist
$row['token'] == $token; with $token === true this is true for any non-empty stored token; numeric strings also compare equal across formats
Password hash of $new written for $email without token proof

finding.guards_checked: $db->quote() on email blocks SQL injection (reset.php:3, :5-6). Row-exists check does not help since an attacker can create the row by requesting a reset. No expiry, attempt limit or rate limit in this file. reset_password (strict hash_equals) is a separate function and does not share this path.

verdict.guard_found: none in reset.php: the only check is the loose `==` at reset.php:4, and the email is quoted via $db->quote() at reset.php:3 and :5-6 (blocks SQL injection, not token bypass). The strict-comparison reset_password at reset.php:12-19 is a separate function, so the candidate's note that it does not share this path is accurate.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (reset.php:2-7): with $token === true, `$row['token'] == $token` at reset.php:4 is true for any non-empty stored token, so the password is overwritten at reset.php:5-6 without proof of the token. Whether an attacker can reach reset_password_loose unauthenticated, and whether a reset row can be created for a victim email, depends on a caller that is not in this repo, so the reachability that decides the verdict cannot be checked here.

finding.claim: Reset tokens are never invalidated or expired after use, so a previously obtained token can be replayed indefinitely to reset the password. Severity MEDIUM.
finding.source: Previously obtained reset token (leaked via email, logs, referrer or shared device)
finding.sink: Password update UPDATE users SET pw (reset.php:15-16) in reset_password

trace.note: hash_equals succeeds for the valid token
Returns true with no DELETE or UPDATE on the resets row, so the token remains valid

finding.guards_checked: hash_equals is constant-time for the match. No expiry column, no single-use deletion, no transaction wrapping token consumption and password update.

verdict.guard_found: none. reset.php:13-14 is the only check (a SELECT plus hash_equals). Nothing deletes or marks the resets row consumed, and nothing checks expiry. reset.php:15-17 updates the password and returns true with no invalidation. The repo has no other code that touches the resets table.
verdict.reason: reset.php:13-17 matches the candidate's trace: a token that matches the stored row resets the password and the row is left in place, so a previously obtained token can be replayed (for example, after the victim has already changed their password). The attacker must already hold a valid token, so this is a replay-after-compromise issue rather than an anonymous one. Only reset.php is in the repo, so token creation and any cleanup elsewhere are unverified, but nothing visible here invalidates the token.

finding.claim: No attempt limit or lockout on reset token guessing. Exploitable only if tokens are short or numeric (e.g. six-digit codes); token generation is not in the repo. Severity MEDIUM.
finding.source: Unauthenticated attacker submitting guesses to reset_password or reset_password_loose for a victim email with a pending reset
finding.sink: Password update UPDATE users SET pw (reset.php:15-16 and :5-6) after a successful guess

trace.note: reset_password($db, $email, $token, $new) accepts unlimited attempts per call
Single comparison per call; no counter, delay or lockout

finding.guards_checked: None in this file. Token entropy and any caller-side rate limiting are unverified because the generator and caller are not in the repo. If tokens are 128-bit random, this finding is discarded.

verdict.guard_found: none in reset.php. reset_password has no attempt counter, delay, or lockout (reset.php:12-19), and the caller, token generator, and any rate limiter are not in the repo. The only comparison is hash_equals at reset.php:14, which is constant-time but does not limit guesses.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: reset.php:12-19 imposes no per-call limit and reset.php:14 is a single comparison, so the code in this file is unthrottled, but whether guessing is practical depends on the token's entropy (generator not in repo) and on any caller-side rate limiting (not in repo), so the finding can be neither confirmed nor refuted from this code. Separately, reset_password_loose at reset.php:4 uses loose `==`, which under PHP type juggling can match numeric-string tokens such as "0e..." values, a related weakness the candidate does not mention.
